newsitem.title: UK: Britain to appoint high-profile "drug tsar".
newsitem.headline: Britain to appoint high-profile "drug tsar".

text.p: Britain is to advertise for a high-profile "drug tsar" to lead the fight against drug abuse, the government said on Wednesday.

Ann Taylor, the minister chairing a cabinet committee coordinating the fight against drug abuse, told parliament on Wednesday the search was on for someone who could bring "visible leadership and drive to the fight against drugs".

The new "drug tsar" -- who will have direct access to Prime Minister Tony Blair -- will be appointed in the autumn for three years to review government action and draw up a new strategy, Taylor said in a written parliamentary answer.
The appointment of a "drug tsar" was a campaign pledge by Labour, which was swept to power in a landslide election victory on May 1.

On Wednesday Home Secretary Jack Straw also unveiled new moves to deal with criminals more rapidly and to impose tougher sentences on repeat offenders. The moves follow a report into the criminal justice system set up by the previous government.

The changes unveiled to parliament include new time limits for cases and automatic life sentences for anyone convicted twice of serious violent or sexual offences and mandatory minimum seven year sentences for repeat drug traffickers.

Straw has come in for criticism from left-wingers for the proposed changes. But, following the lead set by Blair when he held the home affairs portfolio before taking over the party leadership, Straw has taken a hard line on drugs and crime.

The new Labour approach, summed up by the phrase "tough on crime, tough on the causes of crime" invented by Blair, has pushed it ahead of the ousted Conservatives in polls as the party seen by voters to have the best law and order policy.

Straw repeated the message on Wednesday, saying crime had soared under the ousted Conservative government, pushing England and Wales to the top of the league of the 11 leading industrialised nations for robbery, assault, burglary and car crime.
